Hi Jamie / Ayesha,

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciate the clear context on your use case (clinical notes summarization + post-visit triage suggestions). I wanted to summarize what we discussed on HIPAA / PHI handling and lay out recommended next steps so your legal/security teams have concrete items to review.

Summary of where Redwood stands (short):
- BAA availability: We can execute a BAA for customers using Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with isolation) and Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem).
- Hosted API: Our standard hosted endpoints are generally not used for PHI production workloads. In limited cases we can support PHI on hosted infrastructure with additional contractual and network controls, but we recommend Dedicated/Private for production PHI.
- SOC 2 / GDPR: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II controls in place and regular GDPR controls; we can share the security overview and evidence artifacts.
- PHI boundaries: We need to confirm what types of PHI will be sent to the model (identifiers, SSNs, free-text clinical notes, images). Important to confirm whether you expect any structured identifiers to be sent.
- Technical controls available: customer-managed KMS keys (HSM integrations), VPC/private control plane, log redaction, KV cache TTL controls and the option to disable persistent caching for PHI-heavy routes.

Requested next steps from your side:
1) Confirm the PHI elements expected in requests (example: full clinical notes vs. de-identified notes) — this determines deployment recommendations.
2) Send over your vendor security questionnaire (or let me know if you prefer we start) — I can loop in security/infra.
3) If you want to move forward with evaluation, let me know preferred deployment (Dedicated vs Private) and target POC timeline.

I'll attach our security overview and a draft BAA for legal to review; I can also populate the VSA if you prefer. If it's helpful, we can do a brief follow-up with our security engineer to walk through the architecture and log/data retention settings.

Best,

Hi all — looping in from security/infra to address the technical questions. Short answers up front, details below.

- SOC 2 / training: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II (effective 2025) and we maintain GDPR controls. We do not use customer data to train public models; any model tuning would be opt-in and contracted.
- BAA: We can sign a BAA. BAAs are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments by default. For Hosted we can evaluate on a case-by-case basis with tightened contract terms and network controls, but it is not our recommended production path for PHI.
- Logs & retention: By default, Redwood does not persist request/response bodies for hosted requests beyond short-lived caching used for routing/latency optimization. We offer a configurable retention policy and an option to disable persistent logging/caching for specific routes handling PHI. We also provide redaction tooling for logs to strip common PHI fields.
- KMS / encryption: We support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, Google KMS) and HSM-backed key storage for Dedicated and Private. Keys can be customer-controlled for encryption-at-rest.
- KV cache & model memory: Persistent KV cache can be disabled for PHI routes; we also have per-route TTL controls so sensitive context isn't kept longer than necessary.
- Model outputs & egress: Important to design prompts to avoid leaking other customers' data; with Dedicated and Private you get strong tenant isolation.

Recommended path for MedCare POC:
1) Start with Redwood Dedicated for the POC so legal can sign a BAA quickly and you get predictable network isolation.
2) Use customer-managed KMS and disable persistent caching on PHI routes.
3) We'll provide a short security walkthrough (30m) next week to show the configurations and walk through the BAA clauses.

I've attached the BAA draft (same as Marissa sent) and our security overview; these are negotiable in typical ways (data retention window, audit rights, subprocessing lists). We'll also fill out your VSA — please send the questionnaire and I'll have our security ops respond directly.

Regards,
